encounters.cc: Brought to the clinic by his son, who reports that his father has become increasingly forgetful over the past year.

lines: Brought to the clinic by his son, who reports that his father has become increasingly forgetful over the past year.
He has misplaced his keys multiple times, gotten lost on familiar walking routes, and recently left the stove on overnight.
The patient insists these incidents are normal aging.
He retired two years ago from his job as a high school principal and now spends most of his time at home reading or watching television.

He used to enjoy crossword puzzles and woodworking but has recently stopped engaging in these hobbies, saying they feel "too complicated." His wife passed away three years ago, and although he initially managed well, his son feels he has become more withdrawn and less socially active over the past 12 months.

lines: Unintentional weight loss and early satiety with vague right upper quadrant discomfort.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with Alzheimer disease diagnosed in January 2020, primary myelofibrosis evaluated in April 2020, and cirrhosis who presents to the Gastroenterology clinic for evaluation of unintentional weight loss and early satiety over the past few months.
He has also noticed vague right upper quadrant discomfort that has slowly worsened.
He denies fever, jaundice, or change in bowel habits.
His last visit was over a year ago, and he has not undergone any recent imaging.

encounters.cc: Worsening memory problems and confabulation six weeks after hospitalization for acute confusion.

lines: Worsening memory problems and confabulation six weeks after hospitalization for acute confusion.
The patient is a 66-year-old male with Alzheimer disease who returns to the neurology clinic for reassessment of cognitive symptoms.
He was hospitalized six weeks ago for severe confusion and unsteady gait.
Since discharge, he has remained forgetful and often repeats the same questions.
He frequently tells elaborate stories about recent events that his sister claims are implausible.
She also reports that he failed to recognize his nephew during a recent family visit, despite previously being very close to him.

encounters.cc: Persistent productive cough for several weeks with fatigue, low-grade fevers, and unintentional weight loss.

lines: Persistent productive cough for several weeks with fatigue, low-grade fevers, and unintentional weight loss.

This 67-year-old male with Alzheimer disease, alcohol use disorder, cirrhosis with hepatocellular carcinoma, primary myelofibrosis, and chronic malnutrition complicated by prior scurvy and Wernicke encephalopathy is brought to the emergency department by his daughter due to persistent productive cough for the past several weeks.
He reports fatigue, low-grade fevers, and unintentional weight loss of about 5 pounds.
His daughter says he occasionally wakes up coughing at night and has been coughing up thick sputum, which he describes as yellowish and sometimes with a bad taste.
He also complains of occasional right-sided chest discomfort that worsens when he coughs.

encounters.cc: Found confused with headache and chest discomfort in mid-January.

lines: Found confused with headache and chest discomfort in mid-January.

The patient, with established Alzheimer disease, severe alcohol use disorder with physiological dependence, cirrhosis with hepatocellular carcinoma under transplant evaluation, primary myelofibrosis, and history of Wernicke encephalopathy and scurvy from chronic malnutrition, is brought to the emergency department in mid-January after his neighbor found him confused and complaining of a headache and chest discomfort.
He denies cough or fever but reports dizziness and vague chest pressure that began earlier in the day.
There is no history of trauma, and no recent medication or substance changes.
